question: tert-Butylbenzene does not give benzoic acid on treatment with acidic KMnO₄. This is because:
option1: The tert-butyl group is a strong electron-donating group that deactivates the aromatic ring, preventing oxidation of the side chain.
option2: The benzylic carbon in tert-butylbenzene is quaternary and lacks a benzylic C–H bond. Oxidation by KMnO₄ requires initial benzylic hydrogen abstraction, so the side chain is resistant to oxidation.
option3: Steric hindrance from the bulky tert-butyl group prevents the approach of the permanganate ion to the aromatic ring.
option4: Acidic KMnO₄ protonates the tert-butyl group, converting it into a stable carbocation that resists further oxidation.
correct_option: The benzylic carbon in tert-butylbenzene is quaternary and lacks a benzylic C–H bond. Oxidation by KMnO₄ requires initial benzylic hydrogen abstraction, so the side chain is resistant to oxidation.
